title.narrative: Documentation of evidence-based HIV stigma reduction in Uganda - Kitovu and Nsambya home care

description.narrative:
CAFOD has partnered with bet365 foundation to scale up stigma reduction responses in its HIV programmes in Uganda. This follows a pilot that was first tried in Ethiopia, Zambia and Mombasa, Kenya over a period of three years. The project titled "evidence responsive HIV stigma reduction project – Uganda" is seeking to promote HIV prevention and treatment services by including stigma reduction in the responses. The project successfully started in November 2014 and will run over a period of one year to close in October 2015
Following successful grant processing and transfer to the partner it was observed that the project budget accrued a surplus of £7,057.48 which mainly resulted from favourable exchange rate gains. It has been agreed after discussions with the two partners, CAFOD project and funding teams and the donor to use this surplus to produce some additional educational/information materials for the communities. Initially this need was identified as a key project closure activity but not budgeted for.
Over the implementation period therefore, partner staff will progressively capture and document unique stigma and discrimination experiences from respondents and good response practices from other change agents including faith leaders. The unique stories and practices will then be followed up later in the year with an overall production of educational materials to inform transformation realised in the lives of the primary stakeholders of this project. The materials will be in the form of a ‘light read’ booklet on the best practices of this project and an audio visual documentary covering the role of faith leaders in stigma reduction. Target audiences of these educational materials will include project beneficiaries, supporters of this work and collaborators as a way of showcasing the project impact on target communities. It is also anticipated that these materials will promote visibility of this project and contribute to HIV stigma advocacy initiatives by all project stakeholders
